part.text:
RANK: TOLLCAP-SID | position=1 | reason=E6/E7 show the shallow prefixes are already saturated (depth-1 survival 1.000, T1 NLL 0) while the behaviour-tilted l1_br collapses to 0.04671 recall versus 0.06207 for l1_br_euclid, and TOLLCAP is the only candidate that edits only levels 2-3, caps every relabel at the quantizer's own eps_rec, and keeps every cell size and prefix count bit-identical (so it cannot repeat either the deviation penalty or the l1_br prefix collapse), with lambda=eps_rec/sigma_A derived and float64/eps safeguards.
RANK: BEHTIE-SNAP | position=2 | reason=E5/E9 support its hyperbolic compression of popularity/radial differences (top-1 mass 0.4375 vs 0.0543; profile overlap 0.5898) and E6/E7 support editing one level >=2 instead of the saturated level 1, and its one-median-quant-error band respects the measured deviation-recall monotonicity, but the arbitrary 0.5/0.5 weights and unguarded sigma_k=0 for singleton codes make it less controlled than TOLLCAP.
RANK: HCAUDIT-SID | position=3 | reason=Its degree-stratified permutation null is the best response to the weak behaviour signal in E9/E11 (0.5898 overlap; 0.0907 vs 0.067 same-prefix), but tau at the 99.5th null percentile plus the degree>=20 filter leaves only ~0.5-2% of 24,556 items eligible and its greedy repair starts at level 1, which E6/E7 show is already trivially survived with zero NLL, so it is likely inert against the best observed 0.06363 recall and the 0.065 gate.
RANK: SHELL-CURV-RQ | position=4 | reason=It edits all three levels including level 1 during Stage-2 with up to 5% flips per level, the broad behaviour tilt that E6 shows degrades recall (l1_br 0.04671 vs l1_br_euclid 0.06207), and its specification is the thinnest ("See SPEC EQUATIONS") with no map ensuring ||b_i||<1 before the Poincare distance and no guard for sparse behaviour centroids, so it is the least grounded and most likely to reproduce the negative rounds.
